newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen steady.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends up in kerb, seen steady.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee closed up 0.05 at 41.30 to the dollar in the kerb market on Monday amid high demand and is likely to open about steady on Tuesday, dealers said.
They said the rupee was in demand because of the bullish stock market. But the dollar, which had come off quite sharply, might attract some buying at these levels, dealers said.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on July 11, was 40.5200/40.7226 rupees against the dollar.
The premium on foreign exchange bearer certificates closed steady at 2.20 percent.
